record.original_question: For Yudovich solutions of the Euler equations, where the velocity field is divergence-free and has bounded vorticity curl u, are particle trajectories analytic in time? If only Gevrey regularity is known, is that Gevrey regularity sharp?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the incompressible Euler equations on a domain in R^2 (or on a smooth bounded planar domain),
  ∂_t u + (u·∇)u = −∇p,   div u = 0,
with initial velocity u_0 having bounded vorticity ω_0 = curl u_0 ∈ L^∞. By Yudovich's theorem there exists a unique global weak solution u with curl u ∈ L^∞_t L^∞_x, and the associated flow map X(t,x) defined by
  d/dt X(t,x) = u(t, X(t,x)),   X(0,x) = x,
is well defined.

Question: For every such Yudovich solution, is the trajectory t ↦ X(t,x) real-analytic in time? Equivalently, is the flow map t ↦ X(t,·) real-analytic as a map into the group of measure-preserving homeomorphisms?

If only Gevrey-class regularity of the trajectories t ↦ X(t,x) can be established (i.e., the trajectories belong to some Gevrey class G^s with s > 1 but are not known to be analytic), determine whether the Gevrey index s obtained is sharp: that is, exhibit either an improvement to a smaller Gevrey index (ultimately analyticity, s = 1), or construct an example of a Yudovich initial datum whose trajectories fail to belong to G^{s'} for any s' < s.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known: for bounded planar domains with smooth boundary, Yudovich-class trajectories are C^∞ in time, and for Gevrey-M boundaries they are Gevrey of order M+2 (Sueur and collaborators). On the whole plane, time-analyticity of Lagrangian trajectories has been established under slightly better-than-continuous vorticity (Chemin, Constantin–Vicol–Kukavica, Frisch–Zheligovsky type results). Full analyticity for general bounded vorticity, and sharpness of the Gevrey index when only Gevrey regularity is available, remain open.

status_evidence.title: Smoothness of the trajectories of ideal fluid particles with Yudovich vorticities in a planar bounded domain
status_evidence.snippet: For Yudovich solutions in a planar bounded domain with smooth (or Gevrey) boundary, trajectories are C^∞ (respectively Gevrey of order M+2).
status_evidence.claim: Partial regularity (C^∞ or Gevrey M+2) of Yudovich trajectories is established under boundary regularity assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Contrast between Lagrangian and Eulerian analytic regularity properties of Euler equations
status_evidence.snippet: Ideal flow with initial vorticity just a little better than continuous has time-analytic Lagrangian trajectories before initial smoothness is lost.
status_evidence.claim: Time-analyticity of trajectories is known under stronger-than-Yudovich regularity assumptions on the vorticity.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Question listed as related open problem on analyticity vs Gevrey sharpness for Yudovich trajectories.
status_evidence.claim: The full analyticity question for general Yudovich solutions, and Gevrey sharpness, is listed as open.
